newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end up on short covering.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures alike, closed mostly higher on short covering support prompted by a lack of selling interest early and expectations cash pork prices will turn up shortly, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.500 cent per lb higher to 0.075 lower with April up 0.350 at 69.425 cents. Pork bellies finished 0.875 cent higher to 0.400 lower with only distant February off and active May up 75.125 cents.
Short covering and expectations that cash pork prices should be near a bottom kept hog futures reinforced gains in the hog pit at the close, traders said.

Expectations are for pork values to rebound as currently low prices should stimulate increased retailer interest in pork. Pork cut-out values on Wednesday fell to the lowest levels since February 20. Once pork prices improve, so will packer demand for hogs, sources said.
The latest CME lean hog index was down $0.09 at $67.23 per cwt and April futures down to 68.700 early.

"They're saying the price got cheap enough on most pork products - (pork) is going to improve next week because pork is cheap and retail interest will be picking up," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

But the gain in April was restricted late by fund rolling. Cargill Investor Services and Refco were doing the "Goldman roll", fund rolling out of April by the Goldman Sachs commodity fund, late. Buying by Refco, Lind-Waldock and local short covering boosted futures early, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought August 72 puts and Refco bought April 70 puts, pit sources added.

Pork bellies traded choppy much of the day but finished strong on further commercial and local short covering prompted by talk of improved demand for fresh bellies. This offset recent heavy storings and turned technicals up, trades said.
"(Trade sources) were talking about the final (USDA) wire being up a cent or so", following a steady to lower print from the USDA at noon, Levitt said.

Trades noted that most of the buying Thursday was by cash interests which prompted local short covering early and again late. Also, the market appeared oversold. Early carryover selling following the break through major technical support Wednesday lacked follow through which turned the market technically up, especially after the recent 10-cent break in futures, they said.
"Chart wise, we may have turned up," one trader said.

Rand Financials, a notable stopper of March deliveries, bought May on the early rally and R.J. O'Brien bought late after being on both sides early. LFG notably bought all day while LIT division of First Options, Prudential Securities and Smith Barney were early sellers, pit sources said.
